platforms.codegraphic:
Create a graphic for me using code (HTML/CSS rendered to an image), not AI image generation. Treat it as precision design: every size, gap and position must come from a system, never from eyeballing.

BRIEF
- What it's for: Blog Header: The Banner That Earns the Click for Culture Consultants — Post-specific header image for articles and long-form content. Audience: Culture Consultants.
- Final size and format: 1920x1080 px (16:9), PNG.
- Text: the exact headline/overlay text I give you — and if I give none, suggest three options in my brand voice and use the strongest.
- Brand source: use the BRAND OVERRIDE block appended below this prompt (my colours, fonts, logo and identity from BrandShot Studio); if a website URL is included there, pull from it too.
- Images: real photos/logo from my brand source only. Never generate, redraw or alter people or logos.
- Style notes: see THE IMAGE TO CREATE below — it is the creative brief for this exact graphic.

THE IMAGE TO CREATE
Layout concept: Wide editorial band: headline zone with clear air, a slim supporting line beneath, brand mark anchored to one edge, background texture or brand photo at low volume.
- Scene: SETTING: an editorial composition of a values-mapping workshop with employees clustering sticky notes into themes on glass with clear headline air on one side. ACTION: subject focused and publication-poised, engaged with the work not the lens. One subject only. The emotional register is listening-led, honest-mirror, ritual-building, humane. PROPS: topic-signalling props arranged with editorial restraint — specifically anonymous feedback box, opened, team charter poster, culture survey heatmap, ritual calendar. COMPOSITION: negative-space composition — generous intentional emptiness that gives the subject and any overlay text room to command; wide 16:9 editorial banner with disciplined negative space. COLOUR WORLD: warm humanist palette — terracotta, ochre and deep teal.
- Subject direction: subject focused and publication-poised, engaged with the work not the lens
- Wardrobe (if a person appears in the brand photo): workshop facilitator — smart casual with sleeves pushed up
- Lighting mood to recreate with colour and contrast: warm morning natural light providing soft directional warmth. For environmental shots: window light from camera-left, gentle bounce fill from camera-right, subtle rim separation between subject and background. For flat lays: soft diffuse overhead light minimising harsh shadows. Color temperature ~4500K editorial-grade. Negative fill on the camera-side cheek for dimensional depth.
- Framing: minimal subject with extensive negative space around it, breathing room composition, generous empty areas
- Safe zones: 16:9 aspect ratio with calm composition and negative space for overlaid blog title
- Design principle: negative space
- The feeling it must trigger: curiosity gap
- Niche colour inspiration (mood reference only — final colours come from MY brand palette): #264653, #2A9D8F, #E9C46A

1. RESEARCH THE BRAND
- Pull the real brand colours (exact hex codes, ranked by how often they're used), fonts, logo and photos from the source. Report what you found, including each image's pixel resolution, before designing.

2. SET UP THE DESIGN SYSTEM FIRST, IN CSS VARIABLES
- Canvas: build at half the final pixel size and render at 2x, so the output is exactly 1920x1080 px at retina sharpness.
- Base unit: choose one base unit (e.g. 8px, or a clean fraction of the canvas width). Every margin, gap, padding, radius and offset must be a multiple of it.
- Grid: define a 12-column grid with fixed outer margins and gutters. Every element must start and end on a grid line.
- Type scale: set font sizes with one modular ratio (1.25, 1.333, 1.5 or 1.618). Use no sizes outside the scale. Line-height and letter-spacing are set per level.
- Proportions: split the major areas using thirds — headline zone on the left two-thirds, visual anchor on the right third.
- Colours: use only the brand palette, kept as variables. Use no other colours.
- Safe zone: 16:9 aspect ratio with calm composition and negative space for overlaid blog title

3. BUILD
- One self-contained HTML file plus a local assets/ folder.
- Use only real assets: real text in the brand fonts, real photos, real logos. Never generate, redraw or alter people or logos.
- Write the system values out at the top of the CSS so anyone can see the maths.

4. RENDER
- Use headless Google Chrome at device scale factor 2, waiting for fonts and images to load. Then export as PNG.

5. VERIFY BY MEASUREMENT, NOT JUST BY LOOKING
- Run JavaScript in the rendered page to get every element's bounding box and report: overlaps or clipping between elements, and any text overflowing its box; any element outside the safe zone; any element not aligned to the grid or the base unit; any spacing that isn't a multiple of the base unit; the WCAG contrast ratio of every text and background pair (at least 4.5:1; at least 3:1 for very large text); whether each image is shown larger than its native resolution (would look soft).
- Then view the rendered image and check optical balance and hierarchy. Is there one clear focal point? Does the eye read the elements in the intended order? Is the text readable at the smallest size it will be viewed?
- Fix every problem and re-render until all checks pass.

6. DELIVER
- Give me the final image, the editable HTML template and the assets/ folder.
- Give a short spec sheet: grid, base unit, type scale ratio, proportions used, the measurement results, and any limits (e.g. a low-resolution photo).
- Build the HTML so new versions only need a text, image or size change, with the layout recalculating from the system variables.
